slides.title: Why polyphenols as food antimicrobials?
slides.notes: Set up the motivation before mechanisms.

slides.title: Polyphenols are bioactive antimicrobial agents
bullets: Recognised as bioactive compounds and antimicrobial agents
Positioned as natural alternatives to synthetic additives
slides.notes: Straight from the abstract: polyphenols (PPs) play a critical role in food safety, preservation, and shelf-life extension. Frame the review's premise — natural preservation.

slides.title: Antimicrobial action traces to their chemistry
bullets: Hydroxyl groups and electron delocalization drive activity
Interact with microbial cell membranes, proteins, and organelles
Form complexes with metal ions — further amplifying activity
slides.notes: The abstract attributes effectiveness predominantly to hydroxyl groups and electron delocalization, plus metal-ion complexation as an amplifier. Keep to what the abstract states; the full paper details structure–activity correlations.

slides.title: One class, several targets
slides.notes: The abstract lists these interaction sites and consequences for foodborne bacteria. Left = structural targets, right = functional consequences.

slides.title: Mechanisms at a glance
slides.notes: A conceptual summary drawn from the abstract's described interaction sites and effects — no numeric data is claimed. This slide is a NATIVE editable PowerPoint table (each cell can be edited), demonstrating that tables are not images.

slides.title: Structure determines mechanism
bullets: Correlates chemical structure with mechanism of action
Multifaceted rather than a single mode of action
slides.notes: This is the review's analytical thread — mapping chemical structure to how each polyphenol acts. Emphasise 'multifaceted' interactions.

slides.title: Implication: natural preservatives
bullets: Potential as innovative natural preservatives in food systems
Eco-friendly, sustainable alternative to synthetic additives
slides.notes: The abstract's forward-looking claim. Note this is the review's stated potential, not a demonstrated head-to-head result — hedge accordingly when presenting.
